searchText: pls correct me where i am wrong... today there is an input throttle of 900 new validators per day. any more and a queue is formed. What is the proposed exit throttle per day before a queue is formed. Is it further quantified to if there was slashing conduct? thx Exit queue logic is the same as entry queue (i.e. `get_validator_churn_limit` in the specs). Slashing is no different, validator gets put in the queue. See also https://github.com/ethereum/annotated-spec/blob/master/phase0/beacon-chain.md#aside-note-on-a-validators-life-cycle thank you. interesting. with the above throttled entry and exit, an investor can know with certainty the +/- yield (eth denominated of course and subject to uptime etc) i would hope someone (if i could code to save my life i would ) will write a withdrawal script (not exit) or maybe this is best left at the consensus client itself. that would allow for the withdrawal of "proceeds" in excess of the core 32 ETH to another wallet for use ... though i suspect there is wisdom in relying on the 24 words to create the transactions that would do that ... having that "power" in the consensus client would be a security risk... See e.g. https://ethresear.ch/t/simple-transfers-of-excess-balance/8263 , and this server for discussions on "excess withdrawal". I would expect it's not highest on the priority list though. ty

excerpts.content: pls correct me where i am wrong... today there is an input throttle of 900 new validators per day. any more and a queue is formed. What is the proposed exit throttle per day before a queue is formed. Is it further quantified to if there was slashing conduct? thx

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: Exit queue logic is the same as entry queue (i.e. `get_validator_churn_limit` in the specs). Slashing is no different, validator gets put in the queue. See also https://github.com/ethereum/annotated-spec/blob/master/phase0/beacon-chain.md#aside-note-on-a-validators-life-cycle
